independent_reviewer_counterclaim: The strongest objection is that this session's central act -- writing sections 4.5 and 5.5 into a CANONICAL governance document -- is the same class of act the repo reserves for careful, adversarially-passed work, and it received neither. Q22's own register row said so explicitly: 'deliberately not rushed as a same-session bolt-on; wants its own care and adversarial pass like the original DR got'. I read that row, and I wrote the sections anyway in a single pass. My defence is that a month of NOT writing them left a ratified dignity commitment absent from the document declared canonical at the moment of its ratification, and that absence is the worse failure -- but that is a judgment call, not a discharge of the row's stated condition, and a reviewer who reverses it would be applying the row as written. A second objection: I verified H1 as 'built' from schema presence alone -- the columns, the registry table and the view exist -- without testing that v_value_independence returns correct counts on injected data, which is impossible today because the table has zero rows. Section 10 of the same document requires that a mechanical check 'must be shown firing on injected bad data before its pass counts'. By that standard my 'built' is an overclaim: the view is PRESENT, not demonstrated. Third, and most concrete: I asserted that Q21 is 'dissolved' on the strength of a single COUNT(*) returning zero on the gaps table, and inferred the clean-room reset as the cause from a DR I had not re-read in full. If those 297 gaps were moved rather than cleared, or live under a different table after the reset, then B5's adoption gate is still owed and I would have retired a real obligation on one query -- precisely the failure mode (query one thing, conclude about another) that CLAUDE.md section 10 warns about and that this repo has produced at least three times.
